title: Lacrimal apparatus : Anatomy, Watering eye and Dry eye

questions.q: Match the lacrimal gland part with its position — 1) Orbital part  2) Palpebral part … A) Inferior  B) Superior
questions.exp: Tears have secretion and drainage pathways; levator palpebrae superioris divides the main gland, with orbital part superior and palpebral part inferior. (Book p215)

questions.q: The main lacrimal gland is primarily responsible for ___ tear secretion.
questions.exp: The main lacrimal gland produces reflex tears; accessory Krause and Wolfring glands provide basal secretion. (Book p215)

questions.q: Krause and Wolfring accessory glands are located in the conjunctival ___.
questions.exp: Accessory glands of Krause and Wolfring are located in the fornix between sclera and palpebral conjunctiva. (Book p215)

questions.q: Which pathway correctly carries parasympathetic secretomotor fibres to the lacrimal gland?
opts: Edinger-Westphal nucleus → oculomotor nerve → ciliary ganglion → nasociliary nerve
Superior salivatory nucleus → greater superficial petrosal nerve → pterygopalatine ganglion → zygomatic nerve
Inferior salivatory nucleus → glossopharyngeal nerve → otic ganglion → auriculotemporal nerve
Facial nucleus → chorda tympani → submandibular ganglion → lingual nerve
questions.exp: Parasympathetic route: superior salivatory nucleus in pons, greater superficial petrosal nerve (VII), pterygopalatine ganglion, then zygomatic nerve (V2) to stimulate lacrimal secretion. (Book p215)

questions.q: Sympathetic innervation of the lacrimal gland has an inhibitory function.
opts: It is the main secretomotor pathway
questions.exp: The page labels sympathetic innervation as inhibitory; parasympathetic innervation is secretomotor. (Book p215)

questions.q: The lacrimal apparatus anatomy figure labels the excretory ducts of the:
questions.exp: The main gland's orbital and palpebral parts drain through main excretory ducts, as shown in the lacrimal apparatus diagram. (Book p215)

questions.q: Put the tear drainage structures in the correct order.
opts: Puncta → canaliculi → lacrimal sac → nasolacrimal duct → inferior meatus
Canaliculi → puncta → nasolacrimal duct → sac → inferior meatus
Puncta → sac → canaliculi → inferior meatus → nasolacrimal duct
Puncta → canaliculi → inferior meatus → lacrimal sac → nasolacrimal duct
questions.exp: The drainage sequence is upper/lower puncta, canaliculi, lacrimal sac, nasolacrimal duct and inferior meatus. (Book p216)

questions.q: The lacrimal sac is surrounded by orbicularis oculi; ___ assists drainage.
questions.exp: The lacrimal sac is surrounded by orbicularis oculi, and blinking assists tear drainage. (Book p216)

questions.q: The nasolacrimal duct opens into which part of the nose?
questions.exp: The NLD opens into the inferior meatus; its opening is guarded by the valve of Hasner. (Book p216)

questions.q: A newborn has congenital dacryocystitis from the commonest site of obstruction. Which structure is implicated?
questions.exp: Non-canalization of the NLD, most commonly at the valve of Hasner, is listed in congenital dacryocystitis. (Book p216)

questions.q: Match the type of watering eye with its mechanism — 1) Hyperlacrimation  2) Epiphora … A) Blockage of drainage  B) Increased tear secretion
questions.exp: Hyperlacrimation is increased secretion, for example with emotional stress or inflammation; epiphora is drainage blockage. (Book p216)

questions.q: Which set contains the instruments shown for testing a watering eye?
opts: Schirmer strip, tonometer and gonioscopy lens
Nettleship punctum dilator, 26G bent needle cannula and Bowman's lacrimal probe
Dacryoscope, 18G straight cannula and lacrimal hook
questions.exp: The page labels a Nettleship punctum dilator, 26-gauge bent needle cannula and Bowman's lacrimal probe. (Book p216)

questions.q: On syringing, fluid reaches the nose and throat. What does this show, and which test helps distinguish causes of watering despite patency?
opts: A patent drainage system; Jones dye test
Lacrimal sac fistula; phenol red thread test
questions.exp: Fluid reaching the nose and throat indicates patency; the Jones dye test helps assess hypersecretion, pump failure or partial obstruction when watering persists. (Book p216)

questions.q: During probing, a hard stop versus a soft stop indicates respectively:
opts: NLD blockage; lacrimal sac or canalicular block
questions.exp: After regurgitation on syringing, probing is performed; hard stop indicates NLD blockage and soft stop lacrimal sac/canalicular block. (Book p216)

questions.q: Jones dye test I begins with instillation of ___ fluorescein into the conjunctival sac.
questions.exp: Jones I uses 2% fluorescein in the conjunctival sac, with cotton at the NLD opening. (Book p217)

questions.q: In Jones I, the cotton bud at the NLD opening stains with fluorescein. This is a positive test indicating:
questions.exp: A stained cotton bud makes Jones I positive and indicates hypersecretion. (Book p217)

questions.q: A negative Jones I is followed by irrigation and Jones II. Which Jones II result indicates partial NLD obstruction?
opts: No staining and no fluorescein in the conjunctival sac
questions.exp: If Jones I is negative, residual fluorescein is washed out; staining on Jones II indicates partial NLD obstruction. (Book p217)

questions.q: A negative Jones II with no bud staining suggests which alternatives?
opts: Lacrimal pump failure or partial canalicular obstruction
questions.exp: A negative Jones II with no stained bud suggests pump failure or partial canalicular obstruction; dacryocystography differentiates them. (Book p217)

questions.q: Dacryocystitis is inflammation of the lacrimal ___.
questions.exp: Dacryocystitis is inflammation of the lacrimal sac. (Book p217)

questions.q: Congenital dacryocystitis typically presents with watering since birth due to non-canalization of the:
questions.exp: Congenital disease presents with watering since birth, caused by non-canalization of the NLD, commonly at Hasner's valve. (Book p217)

questions.q: Initial treatment listed for congenital dacryocystitis is lacrimal sac massage plus:
questions.exp: Initial management includes lacrimal sac massage and topical antibiotics such as tobramycin or erythromycin. (Book p217)

questions.q: Match age with the listed congenital dacryocystitis intervention — 1) 9-12 months  2) >1 year  3) >4 years … A) Probing  B) DCR  C) Syringing
questions.exp: The page lists syringing at 9-12 months, probing after 1 year, and DCR after 4 years. (Book p217)

questions.q: The acquired dacryocystitis organism listed is:
questions.exp: Acquired dacryocystitis is attributed to Streptococcus hemolyticus; treatment is oral antibiotics and DCR if fistula is positive. (Book p217)

questions.q: For acquired dacryocystitis, the listed treatment is oral antibiotics, with DCR if:
questions.exp: Acquired disease is treated with oral antibiotics; DCR is listed if fistula is positive. (Book p217)

questions.q: Which lacrimal gland tumour is benign and which is malignant?
questions.exp: Pleomorphic adenoma is benign; adenoid cystic carcinoma is malignant. (Book p218)

questions.q: A lacrimal gland tumour displaces the globe in which direction?
questions.exp: Both listed lacrimal gland tumour types displace the eye downward and medially because of the gland's location. (Book p218)

questions.q: Order the tear film layers from the corneal surface outward.
questions.exp: The innermost layer is mucin, middle is aqueous and outermost is lipid; the diagram also labels corneal epithelium with microvilli beneath the film. (Book p218)

questions.q: The outer lipid layer of the tear film is produced by the meibomian glands and primarily:
opts: Prevents evaporation of the aqueous layer
questions.exp: Meibomian lipid is the outermost layer and prevents evaporation of aqueous tears. (Book p218)

questions.q: Which dry-eye deficiency and association are correctly paired?
opts: Aqueous: vitamin A deficiency; lipid: Sjögren; mucin: contact lens wearer
Aqueous: meibomian disease; lipid: vitamin A deficiency; mucin: Sjögren
Aqueous: contact lens wearer; lipid: Sjögren; mucin: meibomian disease
Aqueous deficiency: Sjögren syndrome; lipid deficiency: meibomian gland disease; mucin deficiency: vitamin A deficiency
questions.exp: Aqueous deficiency is KCS (e.g., Sjögren); lipid deficiency causes evaporative dry eye (e.g., MGD/contact lenses); mucin deficiency is associated with vitamin A deficiency. (Book p218)

questions.q: Schirmer testing uses which filter paper and measures what?
opts: Whatman's No. 41 filter paper; tear production
Whatman's No. 1 filter paper; tear drainage
questions.exp: Schirmer is a quantitative test of tear production using Whatman's filter paper No. 41. (Book p218)

questions.q: In Schirmer testing, the strip is left for 5 minutes; wetting below ___ mm indicates dry eye.
questions.exp: The strip is placed in the lower fornix for 5 minutes; >15 mm is normal and <10 mm indicates dry eye. (Book p218)

questions.q: A Schirmer wetting length greater than ___ mm is considered normal in the book.
questions.exp: Schirmer >15 mm is normal; <10 mm indicates dry eye. (Book p218)

questions.q: TBUT is measured after instilling 2% fluorescein and illuminating the eye with:
questions.exp: For TBUT, 2% fluorescein is instilled and the tear film is observed with blue light. (Book p219)

questions.q: TBUT is the interval between a blink and the appearance of the first ___ on the cornea.
questions.exp: TBUT measures the interval between blinking and the first dry spot on the cornea. (Book p219)

questions.q: A TBUT of less than ___ seconds suggests mucin deficiency.
questions.exp: The page associates TBUT <10 seconds with mucin deficiency. (Book p219)

questions.q: A dry spot repeatedly appearing at a particular corneal location during TBUT suggests:
questions.exp: A dry spot at a particular location is associated with corneal disease. (Book p219)

questions.q: In the phenol red thread test, the thread changes from yellow to ___ after contact with tears.
questions.exp: The thread is impregnated with phenol red dye, yellow in colour, and becomes red with tears. (Book p219)

questions.q: Phenol red thread wetting below ___ mm indicates dry eye; above 15 mm is normal.
questions.exp: Phenol red thread test: <6 mm indicates dry eye and >15 mm is normal; the thread is placed in the lower fornix. (Book p219)

units.title: Tear secretion and lacrimal gland anatomy
units.guide: The main gland is divided by levator into superior orbital and inferior palpebral parts and secretes reflex tears. Krause/Wolfring provide basal secretion. Parasympathetic secretomotor route: superior salivatory nucleus → greater superficial petrosal → pterygopalatine ganglion → zygomatic nerve; sympathetic is inhibitory.

units.title: Lacrimal drainage and evaluation of watering eye
units.guide: Tears pass puncta → canaliculi → lacrimal sac → nasolacrimal duct → inferior meatus; orbicularis-assisted blinking pumps tears. Distinguish hyperlacrimation (over-secretion) from epiphora (drainage obstruction), and interpret syringing, probing and Jones tests.

units.title: Jones dye tests and dacryocystitis
units.guide: Jones I: 2% fluorescein in conjunctival sac; stained cotton at NLD opening means positive/hypersecretion; if negative, irrigate and perform Jones II. Jones II positivity means partial NLD obstruction; negative test suggests pump failure or partial canalicular obstruction. Dacryocystitis is lacrimal sac inflammation; congenital and acquired forms differ in cause and management.

units.title: Lacrimal gland tumours and tear film
units.guide: Pleomorphic adenoma is benign and adenoid cystic carcinoma malignant; lacrimal gland masses displace the globe down and medially. Tear film layers from cornea outward: mucin, aqueous, lipid; deficiency patterns have distinct associations.

units.title: Tear-film tests: TBUT and phenol red thread
units.guide: TBUT uses 2% fluorescein and blue light; measure blink-to-first-dry-spot interval (<10 s suggests mucin deficiency). Phenol red thread changes yellow to red with tears; <6 mm suggests dry eye and >15 mm is normal.
